'''Ledick Firest''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] [[Cold-weather Soldier|cold-weather]] [[Rebel trooper|soldier]] who served as a [[colonel]]<ref name="Disney Infinity">''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]''</ref> in the [[Alliance Military|military]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="ESB" /> In the [[Standard year|year]] [[3 ABY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' establishes that the events of [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] occur in [[3 ABY]].</ref> Firest was with the Rebel forces stationed at [[Echo Base]] on the [[planet]] [[Hoth]] when the [[Galactic Empire]] [[Battle of Hoth|attacked]]. He was amongst the troops deployed into the trenches to hold off the Imperial forces while Echo Base was evacuated. After the<ref name="ESB" /> [[T-47 airspeeder]]s<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> of [[Rogue Squadron]] managed to down [[Blizzard 2|one]] of the Empire's [[All Terrain Armored Transport]], Firest yelled to the troops around him to charge the vulnerable [[walker]]; however, the Imperial vehicle was then destroyed by the [[airspeeder]]s in a fiery explosion.<ref name="ESB" />

==Behind the scenes==
The name Ledick Firest first appeared in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] board game ''[[Assault on Hoth]]'' in [[1988]]<ref name="Assault on Hoth">''[[Assault on Hoth]]''</ref> and in [[2013]] was retroactively applied by the [[The Official Star Wars Fact File Part 5 (2013)|fifth issue]] of [[De Agostini]]'s relaunched [[The Official Star Wars Fact File (2013)|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'']] to an unnamed Alliance officer<ref name="Fact File">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File Part 5 (2013)|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' Part 5 (2013)]]</ref> portrayed by an uncredited extra in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], which was released in [[1980]].<ref name="ESB" /> The name was then first used in [[canon]] by the video game ''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]'' when it was released on [[August 30]], [[2015]].<ref name="Disney Infinity" /> Despite the game's non-canon status, [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Pablo Hidalgo]] confirmed on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] that the names it uses for film characters are considered canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/749616406245699584|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2016-07-03|quote=@LelalMekha Yeah, same with Infinity.|archivefile=File:PabloHidalgo-LegoName-Twitter.png|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: "@pablohidalgo <nowiki>youtube.com/watch?v=JwxAeHPLpPg</nowiki> The Lego game identifies a few BG characters from TFA, but are those names canonical?"}}</ref>
